blocks.text: The word "свой" is declined like "мой". The preposition "с" becomes "со" before the word "свой": со своего стола, со своим братом. The possessive "свой" indicates that the object belongs to the performer of the action: *Я взял свои книги. Он взял свои книги. Вы взяли свои книги.*

a) When the performer of the action is in the 3rd person: 1) the possessives "его, её, их" are used if the object does not belong to the performer of the action; 2) if the object belongs to the performer of the action, the possessive "свой" must be used: *Он говорил с его женой* (someone else's, not his own). *Он говорил со своей женой* (his own wife). b) When the performer of the action is the 1st or 2nd person either "мой, твой, наш, ваш" or "свой" may be used without any change of meaning: *Я взял мою книгу.* or *Я взял свою книгу.* c) As a rule "свой" modifies the object only.
From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 49.

The exercises are real sentences: from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR), with their English translations, and from the public-domain Russian books in this library, with author and title. The word in brackets is the dictionary form of the missing word.
